claim: In the matching retail DLL, FormAnimator.PlayAnimationSE (0x06004E7D) is a parameterless 364-byte method. It reads the current FormDispInfo.seID and returns when that value is zero; otherwise it loads MatchSEParam, conditionally calls Ring.ShakeMat when shakeMatLevel is positive and Ring.inst is present, then dispatches exact numeric values: 60 calls ThrowInWeapon, 61 calls Process_ShakeCage and Ring.ShakeCage, 62 calls ReqRopeAction(4,0.5f), 63 searches for a weapon and when an index is found calls EquipWeapon(index) followed by SetAIActCounter(1), 1 calls PlayWrestlerVoice, 6 calls PlayStepSE, and other nonzero values call MatchMisc.PlayMatchSE(seID,1.0f,plObj.PlIdx). CAP-R6-001 contains 45,458 paired PlayAnimationSE executions. 45,447 have no traced direct child and 11 contain one direct Player.EquipWeapon child. Player.EquipWeapon has exactly one callsite in this matching PlayAnimationSE body, inside the numeric-63 dispatch. In all 11 observed child calls, parent and child PRE weaponIdx are -1, child owner_slot equals parent owner_slot, the child raw argument equals child POST weaponIdx, and parent POST weaponIdx equals that same child argument.
